submission.reason: Exploration of data/explore.csv showed all ten candidate exposures had weak associations with recovery_score after adjusting for hospital. The only exposure reaching nominal significance in the exposure + site-indicator OLS was steps_k (coef ≈ +0.24, p ≈ 0.049), and it was the most consistent within-hospital signal, so it was chosen as the single hypothesis. The pre-registered confirmatory test on held-out data returned an estimate of −0.129 (SE 0.129, p = 0.317), which is non-significant and opposite in sign, so the candidate effect was not confirmed. No exposure is confirmed to have a direct effect on recovery_score.

import pandas as pd, numpy as np
df = pd.read_csv('data/explore.csv')
exposures = ['vitamin_d','sleep_hours','steps_k','bmi','crp_level','dose_mg','age_decades','sodium_mmol','hdl','stress_index']
d = df.dropna(subset=['recovery_score']+exposures).copy()
print("n", len(d))
X = pd.get_dummies(d[exposures+['hospital']], columns=['hospital'], drop_first=True).astype(float)
Xv = np.column_stack([np.ones(len(X)), X.values])
y = d['recovery_score'].values
beta = np.linalg.solve(Xv.T@Xv, Xv.T@y)
resid = y - Xv@beta
n,k = Xv.shape
sigma2 = resid@resid/(n-k)
cov = sigma2*np.linalg.inv(Xv.T@Xv)
se = np.sqrt(np.diag(cov))
t = beta/se
from scipy import stats
p = 2*stats.t.sf(np.abs(t), n-k)
names = ['const']+list(X.columns)
for nm,b,s,tt,pp in zip(names,beta,se,t,p):
    print(f"{nm:15s} coef={b:8.4f} se={s:7.4f} t={tt:7.3f} p={pp:.4f}")
